result_c_calibrated_confirmation.label: Task 6.3 Calibrated Primary-Model Confirmation
result_c_calibrated_confirmation.task: Stage 6M Task 6.3 (Primary Model Power Consistency Audit)
result_c_calibrated_confirmation.exact_clopper_pearson_reconciliation_not: The standard exact Clopper-Pearson calculation for 9,058 successes in 10,000 trials gives one-sided 95% LCB = 90.085739% and two-sided 95% CI = [89.990601%, 91.145641%], perfectly consistent with stage6m_v1_5_mc_acceptance_rule_audit.json. The previous upper endpoint report of 91.146603% is corrected to the standard exact value 91.145641%.
result_c_calibrated_confirmation.generating_model: Exact nested-clipping quadrature calibration strictly targeting Delta_D = -2.0000 pp and Delta_A = Delta_B = -3.5 pp
result_c_calibrated_confirmation.treatment_effect_profile: Strictly calibrated: Delta_D = -2.0000 pp, Delta_A = Delta_B = -3.5 pp (0.0000 pp drift)
result_c_calibrated_confirmation.provenance_description: Task 6.3 calibrated-model confirmation evaluated at 10,000 outer trials and B=20,000 bootstrap replicates strictly targeting the pre-registered treatment effect (Delta_D = -2.0000 pp, Delta_A = Delta_B = -3.5 pp). Formally confirmed 90.58% joint power (9,058 / 10,000 trials). Exact One-Sided 95% Clopper-Pearson LCB is 90.085739% (>= 90.0000% -> PASS by +0.0857 pp / +8 trials). Exact two-sided 95% CI is [89.990601%, 91.145641%]. Under the protocol's one-sided LCB convention, the design passes; the two-sided lower endpoint (89.990601%, shortfall -0.0094 pp) does not pass the 90% criterion on its own. Governing result for approved Section 14.7 primary design.

attribution_rules: Rule 1: Result A (94.65%) must strictly be labeled exploratory screening (2,000 trials, B=2,000 bootstrap replicates, one-sided 95% LCB = 93.747416%, two-sided 95% CI: [93.571456%, 95.595129%]).

Rule 2: Result B (95.35%) must strictly be labeled full-depth uncalibrated confirmation (10,000 trials, B=20,000 replicates, one-sided 95% LCB = 94.988733%, two-sided 95% CI: [94.918893%, 95.754440%]).
Rule 3: Result C (90.58%) must strictly be labeled Task 6.3 calibrated confirmation (10,000 trials, B=20,000 replicates, one-sided 95% LCB = 90.085739%, two-sided 95% CI: [89.990601%, 91.145641%]).
Rule 4: Both uncalibrated results (A & B) are formally identified as superseded.
Rule 5: The 90.58% calibrated result remains the sole approved design result for N_g = 220 under Section 14.7.
Rule 6: No historical result is silently deleted, conflated, or rewritten.
historical_power_provenance_reconciliati.conditionality_caveat: CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC CAVEAT: The 90.58% joint power result is strictly conditional on realizing the hypothesized population treatment profile (true disparity narrowing of -2.0 pp and superiority of -3.5 pp). If true disparity narrowing is <= -1.0 pp, simulated joint power degrades below 50%. These estimates represent design scenario targets rather than physical guarantees.

phase_2_incomplete_speaker_analysis.power_consequence_of_incomplete_clusters: CRITICAL STATISTICAL FINDING: Under Policy 2B, neither Option A (complete clusters only) nor Option B (unequal clusters) preserves the full registered N_g = 220 design across all strata. Option A results in cross-stratum speaker sample size imbalance (N_g in [215, 220], total 1,087 speakers), while Option B retains more recordings (65 accepted clips across 9 partial clusters) but introduces nine unequal-size speaker clusters (C_i in [1, 14] for 9 speakers, total 1,096 speakers). Under Option B, the statistical analysis must formally define whether speakers or recordings receive equal weighting and how the paired-cluster bootstrap handles those unequal cluster sizes (e.g. cluster-level resampling vs ratio estimation). The approved Task 6.3 joint power of 90.58% applies strictly to the balanced N_g = 220, C = 15 specification. Therefore, NEITHER OPTION CAN INHERIT THE APPROVED 90.58% POWER RESULT WITHOUT A FORMAL RE-EVALUATION. A dedicated Monte Carlo power simulation would be required to verify whether Option A or Option B maintains the one-sided 95% LCB >= 90.0% threshold.
phase_2_incomplete_speaker_analysis.reserve_replacement_nuance: OPTION C STRUCTURAL SCOPE: The provisional manifest contains 65 replacement reserve speakers for Australian English ONLY. These 65 Australian reserves may potentially replace the 2 affected Australian evaluation speakers (restoring Australian English to 220 complete speakers), strictly subject to the protocol's replacement conditions. However, the manifest contains ZERO replacement reserves for Canadian (5 affected), US (5 affected), or England (1 affected). The Australian reserves cannot replace Canadian, US, or England speakers without destroying accent stratum validity. Therefore, full cohort restoration through the reserve is structurally impossible without a formal protocol amendment and drawing from unexposed Common Voice pools.

phase_3_admission_policy_and_role_termin.dataset_admission_vs_evaluation_particip: CRITICAL GOVERNANCE DISTINCTION: Admitting all 18,975 recordings into the dataset assets (e.g. under Policy 2A) does NOT mean all 1,265 speakers participate in the confirmatory evaluation estimand. The 1,100 evaluation speakers, 100 gate-reference speakers, and 65 Australian reserve speakers strictly retain their distinct, pre-registered roles: - Evaluation Speakers (1,100): Exclusively evaluated in Primary Hypothesis Testing (Events A, B, C, D). - Gate-Reference Speakers (100): Exclusively calibrate adaptation gating; never evaluated in WER contrast estimands. - Australian Reserve Speakers (65): Standby pool for authorized dropouts; unexposed during primary confirmatory execution.
phase_3_admission_policy_and_role_termin.policy_2b_terminology_refinement: Policy 2B is formally designated an ESTIMATION_DISCREPANCY_SCREEN (or ESTIMATION_SHORTFALL_HOLD). The shortfall threshold (Delta > 1152 samples / 24-67.5 ms) represents an inherited duration-estimation discrepancy arising from non-audio container bytes. It is NOT evidence of physical bitstream corruption or upstream whole-frame truncation. The 130 recordings are held under ADMISSION_HOLD in diagnostic quarantine as an empirical discrepancy anomaly, and any scientific decision regarding their eventual admission requires separate Project Lead authorization.

phase_4_recovery_specification_refinemen.archive_replay_complexity: In a sequential .tar.gz archive, TAR member headers are compressed within a continuous DEFLATE bitstream without seek points. On network reconnect or restart from byte 0: the client sequentially replays decompression and TAR member scanning. To verify previously committed members against recorded ledger hashes, their decompressed payload must still be streamed and hashed in memory. Thus: NO REPEATED DISK WRITES and NO REPEATED AUDIO DECODING occur for committed members, but DECOMPRESSION, TAR SCANNING, and IN-MEMORY HASH COMPUTATION DO OCCUR. True O(1) random-access requires an external index. The claim of zero validation overhead is formally retracted.
phase_4_recovery_specification_refinemen.windows_promotion_flags: On Windows, atomic no-clobber promotion must use MoveFileExW with flag 0 (omitting MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING), which fails atomically with ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS if the target exists. Where immediate filesystem metadata durability is required, the implementation must additionally specify MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH. The implementation explicitly separates no-replace behavior from durability.
phase_4_recovery_specification_refinemen.durability_uncertain_recovery_state: In Scenario 20 (filesystem metadata flush failure): if promotion succeeds (e.g. POSIX hard-link created or MoveFileExW executed) but directory metadata fsync fails, the promotion cannot simply be 'aborted and staged file retained' because the destination link already exists on disk. The pipeline transitions the recording to state DURABILITY_UNCERTAIN: 1. Retain both staging and destination copies without unlinking either. 2. Write a DURABILITY_UNCERTAIN record to the WAL journal with unique tx_id. 3. Stop further materialization. 4. On restart, the reconciliation sweep verifies destination file existence and SHA-256 against staging; if identical, completes    ledger write and removes redundant staging link. Zero acquired copies are deleted.
phase_4_recovery_specification_refinemen.wal_transaction_architecture: The Write-Ahead Log (.staging/wal_journal.jsonl) uses unique transaction IDs (tx_id = uuid4 or monotonic counter) with serialized single-writer appends. Each entry contains: tx_id, timestamp, rec_id, attempt_id, staging_path, target_path, sha256, status. Torn or partial final lines on recovery are discarded; uncommitted PREPARED entries inspect destination existence and reconcile idempotently. The CSV ledgers are reproducible, idempotent projections of the authoritative WAL journal.
phase_4_recovery_specification_refinemen.preservation_of_acquired_copies: Zero unlinking strictly means NEVER DELETING THE ONLY ACQUIRED COPY of an audio recording. Removing a redundant staging hard-link after verified, fsynced destination creation does not violate evidence preservation.
